GitHub now reports **all five PRs MERGEABLE/CLEAN** (#20, #21, #22, #23, #24). The remaining piece is the exhaustive verification workflow — once it confirms the 120-order proof, content preservation, and the integration build, I'll deliver the full report.

All merge conflicts are fixed, and every one of the five open PRs is now **MERGEABLE/CLEAN on GitHub** — you can merge them in **any order** with zero conflicts.

## What was wrong

When you merged #17–19 an hour ago, main gained the scaffold-era learning docs, which put the remaining branches into conflict — and worse, #20/#21/#24 all edit `docs/learning/PROGRESS.md`, so fixing each against today's main would still have re-broken the others after every merge. All conflicts were docs-only (`PROGRESS.md` on #20/#21; `GLOSSARY.md` + `index.html` on #24); no code overlapped anywhere.

## What I did

1. Composed **canonical union files** mechanically from the real branch blobs — PROGRESS (Covered: 0001, 0006, 0008; Backlog: 0003–0005 plus all three pending teach-targets from #17/#20/#21), GLOSSARY (all vocab sections), and index.html regenerated for the full 6-lesson set.
2. Merged `origin/main` into each of the three conflicted branches, resolving with those canonical files — so all three now carry **byte-identical** learning docs, which is what makes the merge order irrelevant. Each got a merge commit explaining this; all three pushed. #22 and #23 needed nothing.

## How it's verified (exhaustively)

- **All 120 possible merge orders** simulated at the git object level: every one clean, and all converge to a **single identical final tree**.
- **Content audit**: every line from every branch's original PROGRESS/GLOSSARY survives in the union — the only two changes are deliberate (a stale `(perf/03)` cross-reference and the now-obsolete "numbering needs reconciling" note, both updated).
- **Full integration test**: all five PRs merged together into a scratch tree, then built and tested — cmake build clean, **ctest 44/44**, **pytest 71 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, and all **3 VHDL parity tests ran under GHDL and passed**. Each branch was also independently built and tested green after its merge commit.

## To merge

Any order works. Suggested: **#20 → #21 → #22 → #23 → #24** (#24 last, so the regenerated learning index lands after the lessons it links to). They're all still drafts — mark each ready when you're satisfied with the review.

Two small post-merge notes:
- Your venv has a stale editable install (its `signals_cpp.so` predates the mm-sim bridge). After merging, run `bash scripts/build_cpp.sh` or `uv pip install -e .` so pytest and the dashboard's microstructure panel pick up the fresh extension.
- The PROGRESS/GLOSSARY union appears in each of the three PRs' diffs (that's the price of order-independence) — the merge commit messages explain it for review context.
